name: Neon
limits: 100 CU-hours/month per project, 10 branches per project, 1 GB storage per project and 20 GB account-wide. Compute scales to zero after 5 minutes idle. No overages on Free.
notes: Serverless Postgres with branching, instant restore and connection pooling. The first query after idle wakes the compute.

name: Supabase
limits: 500 MB database and 1 GB file storage per project, 5 GB egress, 50,000 MAU. Free projects pause after 7 days of inactivity. Two active free projects.
notes: Postgres plus Auth, Storage, Realtime and Edge Functions. Paused projects can be restored for up to one year.

name: Nhost
limits: One active project per organization, 1 GB Postgres, 1 GB file storage and 5 GB egress. Project pauses after 1 week of inactivity. 2 shared vCPU and 1 GiB RAM across services.
notes: Postgres with Auth, GraphQL, Storage, Functions and Realtime. A focused Supabase alternative with one free project.

name: Prisma Postgres
limits: 200,000 operations/month, 500 MB storage and up to 50 databases. 10 pooled and 10 direct connections. Databases stop accepting queries when the quota runs out.
notes: Serverless Postgres built for Prisma ORM, with Studio and a one-time 24-hour grace period for exports. No card required.

name: CockroachDB Cloud
limits: $15/month free resource credit equals 50M Request Units and 10 GiB storage across Basic clusters. Single region. Usage above the credit is billed.
notes: Horizontally scalable SQL with serializable transactions and managed backups. The free allowance is monthly and account-wide.

name: TiDB Cloud Starter
limits: Per instance: 5 GiB row storage, 5 GiB columnar storage and 50M Request Units/month. Up to five free instances; 256 MiB memory per query. New connections are refused when the quota is exhausted.
notes: MySQL-compatible HTAP database with vector and full-text search. Strong for analytical workloads and mixed OLTP/OLAP demos.

name: Aiven
limits: PostgreSQL and MySQL: 1 GB RAM, 1 GB disk, 20 connections, single node. Valkey: 1 GB RAM. OpenSearch: 4 GB RAM and 20 GB storage. One free service per engine; services may power off after inactivity.
notes: Managed open-source databases with backups and monitoring. One account can run a free Postgres, MySQL, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch service.

name: Render
limits: Free Postgres expires 30 days after creation, with a 14-day grace period before deletion. 1 GB storage, one free database per workspace, no managed backups or connection pooling.
notes: Useful for short-lived demos, tests and prototypes, not for data you need to keep. Free web services share 750 instance hours and 5 GB bandwidth.

name: Cloudflare D1
limits: Free Workers plan: 10 databases, 500 MB each and 5 GB total. 5M rows read and 100k rows written per day; 50 queries per Worker invocation. Queries fail after the daily limit until midnight UTC.
notes: Serverless SQLite built for Workers, with read replication and Time Travel restore. Daily row limits, not storage, usually bite first.

name: Turso
limits: 5 GB storage, 500M rows read and 10M rows written per month, 3 GB syncs, 100 databases. Databases are blocked when any free quota is exceeded.
notes: libSQL/SQLite with embedded replicas, branching and multi-region reads. Good for edge apps and per-tenant databases.

name: SQLite Cloud
limits: Free plan: 1 CPU, 256 MB RAM, 512 MB storage, 20 concurrent connections and 500k edge function invocations/month. No snapshots; 1-day log retention.
notes: Managed SQLite with REST APIs, auth, row-level security, vector search and offline sync. A more traditional hosted SQLite service.

name: MongoDB Atlas
transfer: 10 GB in / 10 GB out per 7 days
limits: 512 MB data plus indexes, 500 connections and about 100 operations/sec. 10 GB in and 10 GB out per rolling 7 days, 100 databases and 500 collections. Clusters pause after 30 days idle.
notes: Mature document database with official drivers and Atlas tooling. Free clusters use shared RAM/CPU and have no backups.

name: Firebase Firestore
limits: 1 GiB stored; 50,000 reads, 20,000 writes and 20,000 deletes per day; 10 GiB/month egress. TTL deletes, PITR, backups and restores require billing.
notes: Serverless document database with realtime listeners, offline SDKs and security rules. Daily quotas reset around midnight Pacific time.

name: IBM Cloudant
limits: Lite plan: 1 GB storage, 20 reads/sec, 10 writes/sec and 5 global queries/sec. Writes are blocked at 1 GB; reads and deletes keep working.
notes: Apache CouchDB-compatible document store with replication and an HTTP API. Well suited to offline-first and sync-heavy apps.

name: Redis Cloud
limits: Free Essentials: 30 MB memory, 30 concurrent connections and 100 ops/sec. 5 GB network bandwidth per month and one database. Best-effort SLA.
notes: Managed Redis for caching, sessions and queues. The 30 MB cap is fine for a prototype but tight for real workloads; no persistence or backups.

name: Upstash Redis
limits: 250 MB data, 500k commands/month and 10 GB bandwidth. 10,000 commands/sec, 10 MB max request and 100 MB max record. Free databases archive after 30 days idle.
notes: Serverless Redis with REST and Redis protocol access, global replication options and per-request pricing beyond the free tier. Daily backups require a paid plan.

name: Neo4j AuraDB Free
limits: AuraDB Free supports up to 200,000 nodes and 400,000 relationships in 1 GB of storage. One database, no SLA and no point-in-time recovery. One backup snapshot at a time.
notes: Managed graph database with Cypher, APOC and graph algorithms. The node and relationship caps fit learning, recommendations and small knowledge graphs.

name: Qdrant Cloud
limits: Free cluster: 0.5 vCPU, 1 GB RAM and 4 GB disk, enough for roughly 1M 768-dimension vectors. Single node, no HA. Suspends after 1 week idle and is deleted after 4 weeks.
notes: Open-source vector database with filtering, hybrid search and a simple API. Good for RAG prototypes and semantic search demos.

name: Pinecone
limits: Starter: 2 GB serverless storage, 2M write units and 1M read units per month, 1 GB egress, 1 project, 5 indexes and 100 namespaces. Reads are blocked after the egress allowance.
notes: Fully managed vector database with sparse, dense and full-text indexes. The free plan is limited to AWS us-east-1 and one project.

name: Zilliz Cloud
limits: Free cluster: 5 GB capacity (about 1M 768-dimension vectors), 2.5M vCUs/month and up to 5 collections. One free cluster per organization; 2 MB/s insert rate.
notes: Managed Milvus with vector search, hybrid search and scalable indexes. A good upgrade path from local Milvus without running infrastructure.

name: InfluxDB Cloud Serverless
limits: Free plan: 2 buckets, 30-day retention, 5 MB write and 300 MB read per 5 minutes. 500 tables per database and 200 columns per table. Longer retention requires a paid plan.
notes: Purpose-built time-series database with SQL, InfluxQL and Flux. Data older than 30 days is discarded on the free plan.

name: SurrealDB Cloud
limits: Free instance: 0.25 vCPU, 1 GB memory, 1 GB storage and 1 GB internet egress per month. Storage cannot be expanded on Free; instances pause after 7 days idle and become read-only above 1 GB.
notes: Multi-model database with SQL, documents, graph and vector search in one engine. The free instance is ideal for prototypes and SurrealQL experiments.
